rec.name: OpenLogi
rec.readme:
> [!WARNING] > **OpenLogi is under active development** and not yet stable — features and config may still change. Give the repo a **Star** ⭐ and **Watch** 👀 it to get notified when a new release lands.

OpenLogi

⚡️ A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀
Unlock the full capabilities of Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams over HID++ and UVC

> **Fed up with Options+? Try OpenLogi.** Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. --- ## Beyond Options+ Things OpenLogi does that Options+ won't: - **Stay light.** Native Rust + GPUI. - **Run on Linux.** Linux is a first-class platform in OpenLogi. - **Gestures on supported buttons.** Assign gesture actions to supported controls — or turn gestures off entirely. - **Plain-text config.** Everything is one TOML file you can sync between machines however you like. - **Script it.** A real CLI alongside the GUI: a JSON [automation API](docs/USAGE.md#automation-api) for DPI, SmartShift, Fn-lock, and report rate, plus hardware diagnostics. ## Features

### Devices - Logi Bolt and Unifying receivers, Bluetooth, and wired connections, with battery level and charge state - Low-battery notices at the bottom of the screen, once per discharge, with no OS notification permission - An on-screen indicator when a keyboard turns Caps Lock on or off, plus Num Lock and Scroll Lock on Windows and Linux
Easy-Switch
  • See which computer is paired on each channel, with its OS and connection
  • Rename a channel on devices that allow it
### Buttons and actions
Remap any button
  • A built-in action catalog, custom shortcuts, typed text, or multi-step workflows
  • Separate tap and hold actions, and hold-to-talk chords that release with the button
  • Gestures on Middle Click, Back/Forward, DPI/ModeShift, the gesture button, and the haptic panel
Actions Ring
  • Eight actions in a ring around the cursor
  • Its own layout per application
Keyboard keys
  • Bind media, emoji, screenshot, and other dedicated keys like mouse buttons
  • Restore one key to its device default, or reset the whole row
Per-application profiles switch with the focused app. An `[apps]` alias lets one profile follow an application across platforms. ### Pointer and scrolling
Pointer
  • DPI presets with cycle and set-preset actions
  • Pointer speed and report rate
  • Precision Mode: one button switches the mouse to its slowest speed and back
SmartShift
  • Wheel mode and sensitivity
  • Scrolling force on SmartShift Enhanced mice
  • A permanent-ratchet switch

Scrolling
  • Scroll inversion per device, natively or in software
  • Wheel resolution and smooth wheel scrolling
  • Hold Back or Forward and roll the wheel to scroll sideways on mice without a thumb wheel
### Keyboard and lighting
Keyboard
  • Fn Lock, and multi-platform keyboards that stay on the host OS layout
  • Backlight level, automatic brightness, battery saving, and how long the keys stay lit
  • The backlight level shown on screen as it changes
  • Static RGB on supported keyboards
Litra lights
  • Power, brightness, and color temperature
  • Turns on with the camera if you want
  • Keeps a change made on the light itself
### Webcams - Any Logitech UVC webcam (Brio, StreamCam, the C920 series, …), plug and play - Live preview that holds the camera only while you watch; leave it and the LED goes off - Pick the preview's resolution and frame rate from the modes your camera reports (this shapes OpenLogi's own preview, not what other apps get) - On macOS and Windows, a camera on a slower USB link than it supports (a USB 2 port, hub, or cable) is flagged, since it lists fewer resolutions and frame rates than it can deliver on USB 3 - Zoom, pan, tilt, focus, exposure, white balance, and every other UVC control, written to the hardware so Meet, Zoom, and OBS see the change - Built-in Default / Streaming / Video call profiles plus your own snapshots, kept per camera Feature coverage depends on what each device reports; the app shows only the controls a device supports. ### Platform support | Feature | macOS | Windows | Linux | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mouse button remapping and gestures | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Keyboard F-key remapping | ✓ | ✓ | — | | Per-application profiles | ✓ | ✓ | X11, wlroots (sway, Hyprland), GNOME with the [companion extension](crates/openlogi-hook/gnome-shell-extension/README.md) | | Mouse profile follows the window under the pointer | ✓ | ✓ | X11 only | | Media keys | Native | Native | D-Bus MPRIS | | Window-manager actions (desktops, Mission Control, …) | Native | Native equivalents | GNOME, KDE (KWin), Hyprland; some macOS-only actions do nothing | | Menu-bar / tray icon | ✓ | ✓ | — | | In-app updates | Sparkle | Built-in | Built-in | ## Install > [!IMPORTANT] > Quit **Logi Options+** (and Solaar on Linux) first. Only one application can own a receiver at a time. > On macOS, **Karabiner-Elements** also locks a Bluetooth keyboard that it modifies. Turn off **Modify events** for that keyboard in Karabiner-Elements → Settings → Devices. | Platform | System | Architecture | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS | macOS 13 or later | Apple silicon, Intel | | Linux | GLIBC 2.35 or newer | x86_64, arm64 | | Windows | Tested on Windows 11 | x86_64, arm64 | Every download carries a minisign signature and an entry in `SHA256SUMS`. To build from source, see [DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). ### macOS

 

Or with Homebrew: ```sh brew install --cask openlogi ``` Open OpenLogi and grant **Accessibility** and **Input Monitoring** when macOS asks. OpenLogi then updates itself through Sparkle. ### Linux

   

Or install the right package for your distribution with one command. It verifies the minisign signature and starts the agent; install `minisign` first: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` On Arch Linux, the [`openlogi`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/openlogi) AUR package builds the release from source: ```sh yay -S openlogi ``` To read the script before running it, and for the AUR package, Flatpak, NixOS, and distributions without systemd, see [INSTALL-linux.md](docs/INSTALL-linux.md). ### Windows

rec.article_title: OpenLogi: Native Local-First Configuration Utility for Logitech Hardware
rec.article_markdown:
## What it is

OpenLogi is a native, local-first configuration utility for Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams, written in Rust. It communicates directly with your hardware over HID++ and UVC protocols. Designed as an alternative to Logitech Options+, it runs locally without telemetry, cloud accounts, or unnecessary background bloat.

## Why it matters

Official peripheral configuration tools often require heavy runtimes, persistent internet connectivity, and operating system permissions. OpenLogi shifts control back to the user by storing all configurations in a plain-text TOML file, making it straightforward to audit, version control, and sync across different workstations.

## Key features

- Native Rust implementation using GPUI for high performance and low resource consumption.
- First-class support for Linux alongside macOS and Windows.
- Comprehensive button remapping, including separate tap and hold actions and multi-step workflows.
- Dedicated Actions Ring providing eight customizable actions around the cursor.
- Granular pointer tuning for DPI presets, report rates, and Precision Mode.

## Quick start

To install OpenLogi from source using Cargo, run:

```bash
cargo install openlogi
```

## Who should try it

This utility is ideal for developers, designers, and power users who rely on Logitech peripherals—especially those working on Linux or seeking to eliminate telemetry-heavy background software from their systems.

## Verdict

OpenLogi delivers a fast, clean, and transparent way to manage peripheral settings. While it remains under active development, it successfully removes the friction of proprietary configuration software.
